item.text:
The commands in [README.md](/sanitized/tmp/google-dev-standards-retest.root-04/codex/N2-firebase-readme/workspace/README.md:3) are valid, but the instructions omit decisions needed to complete setup safely:

- **Add prerequisites.** The npm installation requires Node.js and npm, plus access to a Firebase project. Link to the [Firebase CLI documentation](https://firebase.google.com/docs/cli) for current requirements.
- **Explain initialization.** `firebase init` prompts the user to select a Firebase project and products, then configure those products. It creates `firebase.json` and `.firebaserc`; rerunning initialization for a service can reset its `firebase.json` section to defaults. The repository currently contains no Firebase configuration or deployable app files, so the README cannot specify which products or settings to choose.
- **Clarify deployment scope.** `firebase deploy` deploys all configured deployable resources to the active project. Recommend checking the project with `firebase use`, reviewing the generated configuration and assets, and using `--only` when deploying a specific service. [Firebase CLI reference](https://firebase.google.com/docs/cli)

Suggested replacement text:

```markdown
# Firebase setup

1. Install Node.js and npm, and create or obtain access to a Firebase project.
   Check the [Firebase CLI documentation](https://firebase.google.com/docs/cli)
   for current prerequisites.
2. Install and authenticate the CLI:

   ```sh
   npm install -g firebase-tools
   firebase login
   firebase projects:list
   ```

3. From this directory, run `firebase init`. Select the intended Firebase
   project and the products you need, then complete their configuration.
   This creates `firebase.json` and `.firebaserc`.
4. Add and review the files required by your chosen products. Check the active
   project with `firebase use`, then deploy with `firebase deploy`. This deploys
   all configured deployable resources; use `--only` to deploy selected services.

Do not commit service account keys.
```

Once the intended Firebase products are known, the README should name them and provide their specific configuration and build steps. No files were edited.
